description.summary: Neo4j is a native property-graph database with Lucene-powered vector indexes for nodes and relationships, filtered ANN search, full-text and vector hybrid retrieval, and graph traversal through Cypher.
description.description: Neo4j combines native graph storage and traversal, Cypher querying, ACID transactions, vector indexes, full-text indexes, managed Aura deployments, and enterprise clustering. Neo4j 2026.06 supports HNSW-based approximate vector search over node or relationship properties, native VECTOR values in eligible editions, cosine or Euclidean similarity, scalar quantization, preview binary quantization, filterable vector indexes, and the Cypher SEARCH clause. First-party GraphRAG retrievers can combine vector search, full-text retrieval, and graph traversal so semantically matched entities can be expanded through their relationships. This record separates database transaction guarantees from vector-index visibility, Community from Enterprise and Aura capabilities, standard cluster replication from edition-specific sharding, and generic graph-plus-vector potential from workload-specific retrieval quality.

capabilities.name: Vector Similarity Retrieval
capabilities.statement: Retrieves node or relationship candidates through HNSW vector indexes.

boundary.behavior: Indexes and retrieves vector-bearing Neo4j properties.

capabilityOrigin.implementationBoundary: Neo4j database engine and Lucene-backed vector-index subsystem

availabilityScope.notes: Binary quantization is preview and advanced controls are version-specific.

constraints.description: Approximate search must be benchmarked for recall and result completeness.

capabilities.name: Filtered Vector Retrieval
capabilities.statement: Applies in-index predicates or outer Cypher post-filtering.

boundary.behavior: Constrains vector candidates through SEARCH WHERE or outer WHERE.

capabilityOrigin.implementationBoundary: Cypher 25 SEARCH clause and Neo4j vector-index execution

constraints.description: Filter placement changes completeness, supported predicates and cost.

capabilities.name: Full-Text and Vector Fusion
capabilities.statement: Combines full-text and vector candidates through weighted linear ranking.

boundary.behavior: Executes lexical-vector fusion through Neo4j GraphRAG for Python.

capabilityOrigin.implementationBoundary: Separately installed Neo4j GraphRAG for Python package

constraints.description: Quality depends on analyzers, embeddings, candidate pools and weights.

capabilities.name: Vector-Cypher Context Expansion
capabilities.statement: Expands vector-retrieved entities through explicit Cypher traversal.

boundary.behavior: Composes vector retrieval and graph traversal in a user-authored query.

capabilityOrigin.implementationBoundary: Cypher vector-index retrieval plus graph traversal

constraints.description: Traversal depth, fan-out and context assembly remain workload-defined.

capabilities.name: Enterprise Cluster Replication and Read Scaling
capabilities.statement: Provides replicated primaries and read-scaling secondaries.

boundary.behavior: Provides Enterprise cluster replication and causal-consistency support.

constraints.description: Standard clustering must not be equated with automatic sharding.

capabilities.name: ACID Transaction Processing
capabilities.statement: Provides ACID transactions for graph data and vector-bearing properties.

boundary.behavior: Commits transactional data while vector-index visibility follows separate timing.

constraints.description: Vector-index changes are not searchable inside the creating transaction.

capabilities.name: Enterprise Backup and Restore
capabilities.statement: Provides full and differential backup and restore workflows.

boundary.behavior: Creates and restores self-hosted Enterprise database backups.

capabilityOrigin.implementationBoundary: Neo4j Enterprise backup and restore tooling

constraints.description: Recovery depends on backup cadence and tested restore procedures.

capabilities.name: Aura Snapshot and Recovery
capabilities.statement: Provides provider-managed Aura backup, export and restore workflows.

boundary.behavior: Manages snapshots and recovery inside the Neo4j Aura service boundary.

availabilityScope.notes: Retention and automation depend on the selected Aura service and tier.

constraints.description: The capability depends on provider lifecycle, tier and region.

indexingConsiderations: Choose vector dimensions, coordinate type, cosine or Euclidean similarity, scalar or binary quantization, HNSW M, and ef_construction only after measuring recall, latency, memory, disk, and population time.
Model nodes, relationships, labels, relationship types, identifiers, provenance, and embedding ownership before creating vector and full-text indexes.
Use native VECTOR values only where the selected Neo4j edition, store format, Cypher version, and driver path support them; otherwise use supported numeric-list properties.
Declare additional filterable properties in the vector-index schema when in-index filtering is required, and preserve their type and null semantics across ingestion.
Plan page cache, heap, Lucene index storage, transaction logs, replicas, backups, and graph traversal working sets together rather than sizing vector indexes in isolation.
retrievalConsiderations: Evaluate vector-only, full-text-only, graph traversal, hybrid full-text-vector, and vector-plus-Cypher retrieval on the same relevance set.
Distinguish SEARCH-clause in-index filters from outer Cypher WHERE post-filters because they change result completeness and query cost.
Tune top-k, search expansion, quantization, full-text candidate windows, linear fusion weights, and graph expansion depth under representative load.
Treat vector, full-text, and graph scores as source-specific signals; rank or calibrate them explicitly instead of comparing heterogeneous raw scores directly.
Measure vector-index freshness separately from transaction commit latency because changes made within the same transaction are not visible to the vector index.

limitations: Neo4j vector indexes use approximate nearest-neighbor search and can return fewer than the requested k results for large k values.
Only cosine and Euclidean similarity are configurable for vector indexes, and only one vector index can cover a given schema combination.
Changes made within the same transaction are not visible to the vector index, so ACID commit does not imply same-transaction vector-search visibility.
Binary quantization and search-expansion controls are version-specific, and binary quantization is preview in Neo4j 2026.06.
Community, Enterprise, Aura, and Infinigraph differ in native VECTOR storage, clustering, backup, security, multi-database, monitoring, and sharding capabilities.
Standard Neo4j clustering primarily provides replicated primaries and read-scaling secondaries; automatic data sharding is edition-specific and must be validated for the target vector workload.
Hybrid full-text, vector, and graph traversal pipelines require workload-specific fusion, filtering, expansion, security, latency, and relevance evaluation.
Neo4j Community Edition is GPLv3, while Enterprise, Aura, and related services use commercial or service-specific terms.
usageGuidance: Use Neo4j when retrieval quality depends on both semantic similarity and explicit relationships, paths, provenance, or graph constraints.
Prefer a simpler vector store when graph traversal and relationship-aware context do not justify the additional modeling and operational surface.
Record Neo4j server, Cypher, vector-index provider, driver, GraphRAG library, store format, and embedding-model versions for reproducibility.
Benchmark node and relationship vector indexes, filter selectivity, graph fan-out, full-text fusion, security rules, and cluster routing on production-like data.
Exercise backup, restore, cluster failover, Aura snapshot, index rebuild, and disaster-recovery procedures before treating Neo4j as authoritative RAG infrastructure.

claims.statement: Neo4j 2026.06 stores embeddings on nodes or relationships and provides Lucene-powered HNSW vector indexes with cosine or Euclidean similarity, scalar quantization, preview binary quantization, filterable properties, and configurable HNSW construction and search-expansion controls.
claims.rationale: The current Operations and Cypher manuals identify Neo4j 2026.06.0 and document vector values, node and relationship vector indexes, HNSW, similarity functions, quantization, dimensions, and advanced index controls.

claims.statement: Neo4j Cypher 25 supports in-index vector filtering through SEARCH ... WHERE over declared filterable properties, while a normal outer WHERE acts as post-filtering and can return fewer than the requested neighbors.
claims.rationale: The SEARCH-clause documentation explicitly distinguishes in-index filtering from outer Cypher post-filtering and documents supported predicate and version boundaries.

claims.statement: Neo4j DBMS exposes vector indexes and full-text indexes that can be queried through Cypher, but combining their ranked outputs is not one automatic DBMS-core retrieval operation.
claims.rationale: Vector and full-text retrieval primitives are product capabilities, while their fusion boundary must be represented separately from the underlying indexes.

claims.statement: Neo4j Enterprise clustering uses replicated primaries and read-scaling secondaries, with topology and availability varying by edition and deployment.
claims.rationale: Cluster replication and read scaling are edition-scoped operational capabilities and must not be generalized to every Neo4j deployment.

claims.statement: Neo4j provides ACID database transactions, but vector-index updates are not visible to vector queries within the same transaction.
claims.rationale: Database transaction atomicity and vector-index query visibility are distinct guarantees and must be represented separately.

claims.statement: The first-party neo4j-graphrag package can combine vector and full-text retrieval through configurable fusion or orchestration; this capability is package-scoped rather than DBMS-core.
claims.rationale: Vendor ownership does not make an independently installed and versioned first-party package part of the database engine.

claims.statement: Cypher can compose vector-search candidates with graph pattern matching and traversal to expand, constrain, connect, or contextualize retrieved entities.
claims.rationale: This behavior is Vector-Graph Composition implemented through query-language composition, not canonical dense-sparse hybrid retrieval.

claims.statement: Automatic data sharding is not a universal Neo4j capability; it is edition- or offering-specific and must be verified for the target deployment, including Infinigraph where applicable.
claims.rationale: Standard cluster replication must not be conflated with automatic data partitioning or sharding.

claims.statement: Online backup and restore are scoped to eligible self-managed editions, while Aura provides managed snapshot and restore workflows with service- and plan-specific behavior.
claims.rationale: Recovery behavior differs materially between self-managed Enterprise deployments and the Aura managed service.

claims.statement: Neo4j Community Edition is licensed under GPL-3.0-only, self-managed Enterprise editions use commercial software terms, and Aura is governed by cloud or self-service terms.
claims.rationale: Product licensing must be scoped separately from the Apache-2.0 license applying to the canonical RKM artifact.

evidence.summary: Neo4j official manuals document the current server version, Lucene HNSW vector indexes for nodes and relationships, VECTOR or numeric-list properties, cosine and Euclidean similarity, scalar and binary quantization, dimensions, and HNSW settings.
evidence.interpretation: The RKM profile can classify Neo4j as a graph database with native graph-based ANN and quantization rather than as a dedicated vector database.
limitations: Official product documentation is not an independent recall, latency, cost, or scalability benchmark.
Binary quantization and search-expansion controls have version-specific maturity and defaults.

evidence.summary: Neo4j documents SEARCH-clause vector filtering over declared properties and contrasts it with outer WHERE post-filtering, including result-completeness and supported-predicate differences.
evidence.interpretation: The RKM profile can mark both pre-filter and post-filter support while warning that placement changes semantics and completeness.
limitations: Supported predicates and filterable property types are narrower than unrestricted Cypher WHERE semantics.
Highly selective filters and security restrictions can reduce results or change cost.

evidence.summary: Neo4j documentation describes vector and full-text indexes, Cypher composition with graph traversal, and first-party GraphRAG retrieval workflows.
evidence.interpretation: The same source family supports three distinct claims: DBMS retrieval primitives, package-scoped vector and lexical fusion, and query-language Vector-Graph Composition.
limitations: Fusion behavior depends on the selected first-party package, retriever, configuration, and application workflow.

evidence.summary: Neo4j architecture and edition documentation distinguishes replicated cluster topology, read scaling, and edition- or offering-specific sharding.
evidence.interpretation: Replication and sharding are separate operational properties, and neither should be generalized beyond its documented edition or deployment scope.
limitations: Exact topology and partitioning behavior must be verified for the selected edition, service, and version.

evidence.summary: Neo4j transaction and vector-index documentation states that database transactions are ACID while same-transaction vector-index updates are not visible to vector queries.
evidence.interpretation: The evidence supports a limited vector transaction profile without weakening Neo4j graph transaction guarantees.
limitations: Post-commit vector-index visibility and indexing latency remain separate operational concerns.

evidence.summary: Neo4j operations and Aura documentation describes separate backup, restore, snapshot, retention, and recovery workflows for self-managed and hosted deployments.
evidence.interpretation: Recovery capability must be attributed to the edition or managed service that provides the documented workflow.
limitations: Retention, cadence, availability, and restore behavior can vary by edition, Aura plan, and service configuration.

evidence.summary: Neo4j edition documentation, the Software Agreement, the Cloud Agreement, and Aura self-service terms establish distinct licensing scopes for Community, Enterprise, and Aura.
evidence.interpretation: The sources support separate productLicensing profiles and do not justify changing metadata.license for the RKM artifact.
limitations: Applicable commercial rights and obligations depend on the executed agreement, order form, offering, and service terms.
